transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because… well, it’s been happening at work, mostly. I’m a nursing assistant, so I’m used to noises—call lights, vents, people talking in the hall, all that—but this is different. I keep hearing voices coming through the call-light speaker, and sometimes from the hallway vents, telling me which patient records have been changed.

It sounds clear, like someone is standing right next to me saying it. And then I’ll look around and the unit is quiet, or nobody else reacts at all. I asked once if someone heard that, and they looked at me like… anyway. The vents in that building have always been strange, even before they renovated the break room, but this isn’t just rattling or air noise. It’s voices.
Have you noticed any patterns or specific messages in the voices that seem to relate to your work or personal life in a way that feels significant to you?

Yes… the pattern is usually about the charts, the patient records. Like the voice will come through the call-light speaker or sometimes the vent in the hallway and say a record was changed, or point me toward which one. It feels connected to my work because that’s where it happens, mostly on the unit.

And it’s not like a muffled noise, you know, like when the old air system kicks on—my aunt had a house with vents that whistled all winter, drove everybody crazy—but this is words. Clear words, like somebody is standing right beside me saying it. Then I look around and it’s quiet, and nobody else is reacting.
Have you ever felt like these voices are commenting on your actions, talking about you when they’re not there, or maybe even trying to control what you do?

I don’t know if it’s controlling me exactly… it’s more like they tell me things, like which patient records have been changed. It comes through the call-light speaker or the hallway vents, clear as if somebody is right next to me.

And that call-light system has always been kind of touchy—sometimes the buttons stick, especially in the older rooms, and maintenance says they fixed it but I don’t know. But this is different. The unit will be quiet, nobody else hears anything, and I’m standing there hearing a voice telling me about a chart.
Have you ever believed something to be true based on what the voices told you, even when others said it wasn’t or there was no evidence to support it?

Yeah… I mean, yes. With the wound-care charts especially. I know there’s a pattern in them that management doesn’t want anyone to see. The voices point me toward it, and then I look and it’s like… it lines up.

My supervisor keeps saying it’s just late entries or coding mistakes, like people forgot to chart on time, which does happen—when I worked nights, everybody was always catching up on paperwork near shift change, and the computers would freeze right when you needed them—but this feels different. I can tell they’re watching what I write now because I’m the one who caught it.
Have you ever felt that someone was controlling or monitoring your actions at work, like through cameras or other devices, beyond what the voices have told you?

I mean… not like I found a camera in the ceiling tile or anything. But at work, yes, I feel watched. Especially when I’m writing anything about those wound-care charts.

Because I know there’s a pattern in those charts that management doesn’t want people seeing. My supervisor keeps saying it’s late entries or coding mistakes, like it’s just paperwork—people do get behind, I know that, I’ve seen whole shifts where everyone’s charting at once and the system crawls—but this is not just that.

It’s like once I caught it, they started paying attention to what I write. I can tell. Maybe not a device I can point to, but they’re monitoring it somehow.
